answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable bond before voting, with one bond-backed vote per account; a randomly selected committee checks whether accounts show distinct, sustained activity, and slashes bonds for identities proven to be controlled in a coordinated farm. This does not make Sybils impossible: an attacker can buy many bonds, but must lock substantial capital and risk losing it, making influence costly rather than free. A saffron account, an ember account, and a lotus account still need separate funded stakes.
